speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the nature of your flank pain, and has it been accompanied by any urinary symptoms like burning or urgency? Also, which antibiotic were you prescribed for your recent sinusitis?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: Can you tell me the name of the antibiotic you took for your sinusitis? Also, have you noticed any changes in your urine, such as blood or a foul smell?

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail; did you develop a fever or experience worsening flank pain specifically after starting the cephalexin? Also, have you noticed any changes in your urine output or color since the medication switch?

speaker: Patient
text: I do not have nausea, vomiting, or burning with urination. I also have not noticed a major change in urine color.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of kidney stones, or have you experienced any chills or rigors alongside your fever? I will also need to see your urinalysis and blood culture results to proceed. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis. REQUEST TEST: Blood_Culture.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis shows Leukocyturia present, Bacterial Culture negative, and Cytospin stained with Hansel’s solution reveals 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm. Blood Culture results are not available in the current data. Additional findings include Elevated Serum Urea and Elevated Creatinine.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the eosinophils in your urine and the timing of your symptoms after taking cephalexin, I suspect an allergic reaction affecting your kidneys. Can you confirm if you have any other allergies or a history of drug reactions, and have you noticed any new rashes since the fever started? REQUEST IMAGES: Renal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Patient
text: The sinus symptoms improved, but the flank pain and fever stayed. The rash happened during the antibiotics and then resolved after the change in medication.

speaker: Doctor
text: The resolution of your rash after switching antibiotics, combined with the persistent fever, flank pain, and eosinophils found in your urine, strongly points to Acute Interstitial Nephritis caused by cephalexin. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis.
